story_review.one_viewing_summary: This is the planned chain, not observed pixels. Brown water tops a San Antonio curb and climbs a fence post to its orange ankle mark while the porch phone stays dark, then the warning lands late. The prototype station at the curb charges from the sun, and its dashed line toward a cell tower stops halfway. Water rises past its four lenses and each lights. The opened housing feeds the chip, which lights a large amber lamp and risk bar while a dark server across the road is never reached. Rings run down a long street to the hub and across open country to its mast. A seated responder works at a flood map whose paths spread along the creek. On a curb notice board the 98.82% card fills and now stays whole through the push, the assessments tag pins and a blank field result card slides in. The next shot then pushes the figure off the left edge to '2%' while a stamp prints none reported. A finger reads a blank paper map, and a technician folds the deployment plan into the prototype's latched case.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The opening asks whether a station can judge rising street water with no power line and no cell tower. The mechanism chain of charge, four lenses, local chip judgment, radio to the hub and flood map answers yes as a design. The limits stay in the curb world: validation accuracy only, no field result, and no installation named. The close keeps the plan with the uninstalled prototype toward the stated goal, so no unreported outcome is promised. One defect undercuts the answer: the validation figure that s7 now shows whole is cut to '2%' in s8-shot-1, exactly where the film says no field result exists.
story_review.weakest_transition: s7 to s8 at 49.2 s. The cut from the corrected detail shot (figure at x 43 to 427) to the two-card view (figure at x 38 to 278) is itself readable. Within about 0.4 s, though, s8-shot-1's push slides the same card off the left edge, so the image that should carry 'the same card beside a blank field result card' instead carries a truncated figure.
